t:
(a) 

Such amounts as may be necessary under the authority and conditions provided in the applicable appropriations Act for the fiscal year 1995 for continuing projects or activities including the costs of direct loans and loan guarantees (not otherwise specifically provided for in this title of this joint resolution) which were conducted in the fiscal year 1995 and for which appropriations, funds, or other authority would be available in the following appropriations Act:

The District of Columbia Appropriations Act, 1996:

Provided, That whenever the amount which would be made available or the authority which would be granted in this Act is greater than that which would be available or granted under current operations, the pertinent project or activity shall be continued at a rate for operations not exceeding the current rate.

 
    (b) 
Whenever the amount which would be made available or the authority which would be granted under the Act listed in this section as passed by the House as of the date of enactment of this joint resolution, is different from that which would be available or granted under such Act as passed by the Senate as of the date of enactment of this joint resolution, the pertinent project or activity shall be continued at a rate for operations not exceeding the current rate or the rate permitted by the action of the House or the Senate, whichever is lower, under the authority and conditions provided in the applicable appropriations Act for the fiscal year 1995: Provided, That where an item is not included in either version or where an item is included in only one version of the Act as passed by both Houses as of the date of enactment of this joint resolution, the pertinent project or activity shall not be continued except as provided for in section 211 or 212 under the appropriation, fund, or authority granted by the applicable appropriations Act for the fiscal year 1995 and under the authority and conditions provided in the applicable appropriations Act for the fiscal year 1995.

fable.w: This is a continuing-resolution funding provision that sets the rate of operations for District of Columbia appropriations by reference to House- and Senate-passed bills. The tempting reading is that the mention of the District of Columbia or of House/Senate action implies outside consultation, but the only actors are the chambers of Congress, which are inside the federal government. It provides no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.
fable.s: the pertinent project or activity shall be continued at a rate for operations not exceeding the current rate or the rate permitted by the action of the House or the Senate, whichever is lower

opus.w: This continuing resolution sets funding rates for District of Columbia projects by comparing fiscal year 1995 authority with the House and Senate versions of the 1996 Act. The only bodies mentioned are the House and Senate, which are inside the federal government, so their actions do not count as participation. No comment period, hearing, consultation with outside parties, advisory body or right to sue is created, and no rulemaking is required or authorized.
opus.s: the pertinent project or activity shall be continued at a rate for operations not exceeding the current rate or the rate permitted by the action of the House or the Senate, whichever is lower
opus.b: The tempting reading would treat "the action of the House or the Senate" as a form of participation. It isn't one: the House and Senate are part of Congress, which is inside the federal government. The section is a continuing appropriations formula for the District of Columbia, and it involves no outside party.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a standard continuing resolution provision that authorizes funding for ongoing projects based on previous appropriations acts. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties, including the District of Columbia government. The reference to the District of Columbia Appropriations Act is solely to identify the specific funding stream, not to establish a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: Such amounts as may be necessary under the authority and conditions provided in the applicable appropriations Act for the fiscal year 1995 for continuing projects or activities including the costs of direct loans and loan guarantees (not otherwise specifically provided for in this title of this joint resolution) which were conducted in the fiscal year 1995 and for which appropriations, funds, or other authority would be available in the following appropriations Act: The District of Columbia Appropriations Act, 1996:
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text mentions the "District of Columbia Appropriations Act," it implies some form of consultation with the District government. However, the text itself is purely a procedural rule for a continuing resolution regarding federal funding levels. It does not mandate any interaction, consultation, or coordination with the District of Columbia government or any other outside entity. The mention of the Act is merely to identify the source of the funding authority.
